sections.h2: Where do I pay and ask about property tax in Monroe County, NY?
sections.html:
In Monroe County, the Treasury Division of the Department of Finance collects fees and taxes at the County Office Building, Room B2, 39 W. Main Street in Rochester, and you can reach it at 585 753-1200. Your town or city tax receiver and your assessor are separate offices, and the county publishes a contact table for both.

Monroe County lies on the southern shore of Lake Ontario, with Rochester as county seat and largest city. The county's own table lists twenty town offices, from Brighton and Chili to Webster and Wheatland, plus the City of Rochester. That is a lot of separate assessors, and each sets values for its own roll, so a house in Pittsford and a house in Greece are assessed by different offices on the same county calendar.

In the City of Rochester, the assessor and the tax receiver both work from City Hall, Room 101-A, at 30 Church Street. Suburban owners deal with their town hall instead, and a few towns share an assessor: the county table shows the same assessor name covering Mendon and East Rochester, and another covering Gates and Ogden.

  • Pay or look up a bill through the county's Real Property Portal, linked from the Treasury page.
  • Ask your town assessor about value, exemptions and Grievance Day.
  • Ask the town or city tax receiver about a bill that has not arrived.

sections.h2: When are Monroe County tax bills due?
sections.html:
The combined town and county bill is mailed by December 31 and is due in full on February 10, or in four installments on February 10, February 28, March 30 and April 30. School bills are mailed by August 31 and are due October 1, with three installment dates of September 15, October 15 and November 15.

The third school installment date, November 15, is today, so a balance left unpaid after it will be treated as unpaid school tax. The county says any unpaid school balance, plus penalty and interest, is re-levied onto the next combined town and county bill. In other words, a school balance you ignore in the fall comes back on the January bill under the county's name.

Owners aged 65 or older, or with a disability, who live in a one- to three-family home can name a trusted adult to receive duplicate bills and unpaid-tax notices. The application deadline each year is November 1, so for 2026 that date has passed.

sections.h2: What happens when Monroe County property tax goes unpaid?
sections.html:
Monroe County runs a long, notice-heavy process that lasts about twenty-eight months before an auction, and it says a signed payment plan in good standing keeps a parcel out of foreclosure. The county's Treasury page lists up to ten notices over that span.

Monroe County unpaid tax steps, from the county Treasury page
Point in the cycleCounty action
Early AprilCourtesy reminder if not paid in full by February 10
MayRequired notice after the April 30 installment date
August 15List of lands with unpaid taxes published by law
August 20Taxes declared delinquent
Following June and August 15Sixth notice, then a second publication
September of the next yearForeclosure auction scheduled after two years of delinquency

Source: Monroe County Treasury / Property Tax. Under the county's In Rem Tax Foreclosure Act, a parcel leaves the list only for full redemption, bankruptcy, a court order, or legislative approval on narrow grounds such as a valid challenge to the lien or an approved repayment agreement.

sections.h2: What are the Monroe County assessment and grievance dates?
sections.html:
Town property is valued as of July 1 and taxable status is March 1, the date exemption applications must be filed. The tentative roll is filed May 1, Grievance Day is the fourth Tuesday of May, and the final roll is signed July 1.

For 2027 the fourth Tuesday of May is May 25, but confirm with your local assessor, as the county itself advises. The City of Rochester runs on a different calendar: its valuation date and taxable status date are both February 1, and its tentative roll comes March 1. A seller in Rochester therefore has an earlier window to challenge value than a seller in a suburban town.

Monroe County also posts its tax rate tables online, including 2026 town and county rates, 2025-26 school rates, 2025 village rates and 2026 special district rates. If you suspect you pay too much, compare your rate lines before you decide whether an appeal is worth the effort.

sections.h2: What do Monroe County homes and owners look like?
sections.html:
Monroe County is the most urban of this group, with 750,506 residents in the Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate and 342,061 housing units on about 657 square miles of land. Owners occupy 63.7% of homes, so rental properties are a large share of the market.

The median owner-occupied home was valued at $213,700 for 2020 to 2024, median household income was $76,382, and median gross rent was $1,173. Eastman Kodak, Paychex and Wegmans are among the employers tied to the area, and about 25 public school districts serve the county, including the Rochester City School District.

The county-wide median hides wide differences between lakeshore suburbs and Rochester neighborhoods, so check your own parcel's assessment and tax rate lines instead of leaning on the average.

Commutes are short by upstate standards, with mean travel time to work of 19.9 minutes, and the Census counts 318,428 households at 2.28 people each. The Census lists 755 building permits for 2025. A written payoff from the Treasury office gives a buyer or title company a firm number to work from.

sections.h2: How do I sell a Monroe County house with tax owed?
sections.html:
Get a current payoff from the Treasury office, then decide whether to pay it, set up a payment plan or sell before the August 15 publication. The county says staff will try to negotiate a plan during the whole process, and housing counseling agencies such as the Urban League of Rochester and The Housing Council are named on its page.

If a plan is not workable, selling can clear the balance from proceeds. A buyer who pays cash and takes the home in its present condition can shorten the timeline, which helps when a publication date or auction schedule is near.

  1. Ask Treasury for a payoff figure for the parcel.
  2. Ask about a payment plan, which the county says protects a parcel while payments stay current.
  3. Compare closing dates with August 15 and the September auction month.

faqs.q: When is the Monroe County town and county tax due?
faqs.a: February 10 is the due date for full payment, with installments due February 10, February 28, March 30 and April 30. The bill is mailed by December 31 to your lender if you escrow, or to you directly.

faqs.q: What is Grievance Day in Monroe County?
faqs.a: It is the fourth Tuesday in May in the towns, which is May 25, 2027. The Board of Assessment Review meets then, and it is the last day to file a formal complaint against a tentative assessment. Confirm locally.

faqs.q: Does Monroe County have a payment plan for back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. County Treasury staff try to negotiate a plan with owners, and the county says a signed plan with no missed payments keeps a parcel out of foreclosure. Call 585 753-1200 to ask.

faqs.q: When does Monroe County list delinquent properties?
faqs.a: By law the list of lands with unpaid taxes is published on August 15, and the county declares taxes delinquent on August 20. A second publication follows if the balance stays unpaid into the next year.

faqs.q: What happens to unpaid school tax in Monroe County?
faqs.a: The unpaid school balance, with penalty and interest, is re-levied as a county tax on the next combined town and county bill. That is why it can show up again in January.
